description: By Olivia MorleyLegislation signed into law this past week provides stricter guidelines for detecting lead poisoning in young children in Georgia. During this past session, state Rep. Katie Dempsey, R-Rome, sponsored a bill that lowered the allowable lead poisoning levels in children from 20 deciliters to 3.5 deciliters. The level is now consistent with guidance from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Georgia Department of Public Health Commissioner Kathleen Toomey approached Dempse
